nodes.label: Agent Teams Console
nodes.rationale: A Claude Code plugin that renders a live browser console for agent teams: every teammate's transcript, the shared task list, mailboxes, context burn, and NEEDS YOU items. Never started manually - the plugin's PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks on the Agent and Workflow tools start the server and print the URL once per team. Everything is local: nothing leaves 127.0.0.1 and cross-origin requests are refused.

nodes.label: Team Mode (six views)
nodes.rationale: Six views: wall (one transcript column per teammate, lead pinned left), overview (context-occupancy tiles), comms (everyone room plus per-pair inbox threads), tasks (shared task list), rail (keyboard-navigable list with one big transcript), grid (six panes for wide monitors).

nodes.label: Workflow Mode
nodes.rationale: Chosen by what triggered the run, not a toggle. A workflow subagent never enters members[], so a workflow is not a team: no roster, no inboxes, no task list, no composer. Four views: run, agents, script, journal. It has no controls and cannot have any: skip-agent and stop-run are an AbortController.abort() plus an in-memory registry write inside the session process; nothing on disk drives them, the per-session unix socket carries no workflow verb, a queued prompt would arrive only after the run ends, and a signal to the pid would kill the whole session. A control whose only effect is its own highlight teaches a capability that does not exist. Checked against Claude Code 2.1.231.

nodes.label: Launcher Wake Gate
nodes.rationale: The launcher runs on every Agent or Workflow tool call, so it is written to be cheap and do nothing almost every time. For an Agent call it reads ~/.claude/teams/<team>/config.json and gives up unless two or more members are listed; every Workflow call wakes the console since a run forms no team. Ordinary subagents, Explore, workflow fan-outs and parallel search agents never appear in members[] (verified in a capture spike with six live workflow subagents), so they cost one short-lived shell process and nothing else.

nodes.label: Ten Observation Hooks
nodes.rationale: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest, UserPromptSubmit, Notification, Stop, SubagentStop, SessionStart, SessionEnd, PreCompact - all registered in plugin/hooks/hooks.json and firing from the plugin, so permission cards, plan approvals and tool activity work on a bare install with no settings.json edit. Each costs one refused connection while the console is not running.

nodes.label: Per-Team Append-Only Event Log
nodes.rationale: agent-teams-console/logs/<team>.jsonl, one file per team so a console started for a second team cannot overwrite the first team's history. Pruned at startup, capped per event kind and per agent for transcript history, dropped after a week untouched. Only mostly rebuildable: roster, transcripts, tasks and mail come back from ~/.claude on the next sweep, but hook-pushed data (status line, per-agent substatus, permission and plan cards) exists nowhere else. A one-time migration folds the old shared events.db into per-team logs, renaming it to events.db.migrated-<epoch-ms>.

nodes.label: Agent Teams Env Vars
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 (without it there are no teams to show) and CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1 (fills the tasks view). They live in settings.json because a plugin manifest has nowhere to put env, and a shell export only reaches sessions started from that shell. Read once at session start, so a restart is required.

nodes.label: subagentStatusLine Key
nodes.rationale: The settings.json key that reports each teammate's current tool into its console header. No plugin-manifest equivalent exists, so /console-setup writes it - but only when the key is absent.

nodes.label: Status Line Non-Takeover Policy
nodes.rationale: The console's statusLine command ends in printf '' - it draws nothing, its job is only to POST the payload. Written over an existing status line (ccstatusline, starship, custom) it would blank the bar, so the install never takes the key unless it is empty; the operator gives up only the rate-limit gauge and the lead's cost/context readouts. Chaining both (POST then hand payload to the user's command) happens only on an explicit request.

nodes.label: Idle Reaper Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: The server exits ten minutes after the last team goes away and immediately on the lead's SessionEnd. The reaper reads only the filesystem and keeps the process alive while any team has two or more members. 'The server stays up' is a description, not a mandate.

nodes.label: plugin/ Install Boundary
nodes.rationale: Everything that ships lives in plugin/ (1.3M); nothing else in the repo is installed. claude plugin install runs npm install when it finds a package.json at the plugin root - an earlier layout put 141M on disk that way - so package.json and src/ stay at the repo root. plugin/dist/ is committed because a plugin is just files and nothing builds on the user's machine; the esbuild bundle has no runtime dependencies and the build is deterministic.
